Subtask 2.1: Electrical testing of encapsulated PSC devices: Unprotected and encapsulated cells were tested continuously near their maximum power point (“quasi- MPP” technique) in a laboratory at 50 °C, in air (40-60% R.H.), 1-sun intensity. Current- voltage measurements were conducted periodically to identify premature degradation. Subtask Summary: To assess the performance of the IZO/TCC as an integrated electrode, PSCs were encapsulated with the semi-bonded Aluzine-based TCC and coated with a secondary-IZO electrode (Figure 23a). PV performances of PSCs were benchmarked with illumination through the Glass/ITO substrate to assess electrical performance without optical effects from the IZO/TCC encapsulation (Figure 23b). Then, PSCs were characterized with illumination through the IZO side (i.e., IZO/TCC for encapsulated PSCs) to assess the optical and electrical performance of the IZO/TCC encapsulation (Figure 23c). A control sample from the same batch of PSCs served as the comparative benchmark, and the results are summarized in Table 12. When illuminated through the glass/ITO substrate, the average open circuit voltage (V , OC 1.153 V) and short-circuit current density (J , 23.04 mA/cm2) of the three AVG SC AVG encapsulated samples measure near coincident to the control device (V : 1.147 V, J : OC SC 23.31 mA/cm2). A substantial and systematic improvement in fill-factor (FF) is observed for the encapsulated devices (FF, 80.59 %) compared to the control device (FF: 77.53 AVG %), and contributes to the higher averaged PCE values of encapsulated devices (PCE, 21.41 %) compared to the control device (PCE: 20.72 %). The slight improvement AVG appears to be related to enhanced charge carrier extraction and transport, attributable to the improved interfacial contact within the multilayered PSC structure due to pressurized lamination during TCC integration.161 Illumination through the IZO/TCC encapsulant results in a slight reduction (approx. 4%) in the averaged J of the encapsulated samples SC (J , 19.6 mA/cm2) compared to the control device (J : 20.33 mA/cm2). The optical SC AVG SC loss, attributed primarily to optical shading, is near the target value of 5% microsphere concentration for this TCC formulation (5±2% Ag-PMMA by area). Despite the slight optical loss, the overall improvement in averaged FF (FF, 78.63 %) compared to the AVG control (FF: 76.07 %) resulted in encapsulated devices maintaining higher PCEs (PCE, 17.59 %) compared to the control device (PCE: 17.46 %).
